newsitem.title: USA: Two potential witnesses questioned in Cosby murder.
newsitem.headline: Two potential witnesses questioned in Cosby murder.

text.p: Police questioned two potential witnesses late on Monday in connection with the murder of entertainer Bill Cosby's son, who was gunned down last week while changing a flat tire near a freeway.

Officer Eduardo Funes, a Los Angeles police spokesman, said investigators were interviewing "two individuals" as part of the murder investigation, but he stressed that neither had been arrested or detained.
Los Angeles TV station KCBS reported the two men had been held briefly by the suburban Torrance police force before being handed over to Los Angeles detectives for questioning.

One of them reportedly fit a recently released composite sketch of a potential witness to Ennis Cosby's murder, which took place early last Thursday on a darkened roadside in an affluent neighbourhood.
Police declined comment on the TV report. Investigators said they had interviewed numerous people as possible witnesses in the case, but so far they have no suspects.
A woman who saw part of the attack gave police a description of the killer as a white male wearing a knit cap, and that was used to put together a composite drawing released last weekend.

In asking for the public's help in identifying a second possible witness to the crime, police said the man they sought was driving a blue hatchback vehicle. KCBS reported the two men being questioned on Monday were in a similar car.
As the investigation continued, the supermarket tabloid the National Enquirer offered a $100,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the killer.
"Mr. (Bill) Cosby has been a long-standing friend of the Enquirer and the Enquirer's family of readers," the weekly newspaper said in a press release.
The Enquirer quoted Cosby as saying: "I urge anyone with any information about my son's death to come forward immediately."
Police have been flooded with calls in response to the composite drawing of the suspect. Ennis Cosby died from a single gunshot to the head. Investigators said robbery was the likely motive.

In another development, a Los Angeles woman and an alleged accomplice were arrested in New York on charges of attempting to extort $40 million from Bill Cosby in exchange for not telling the media she was his illegitimate daughter, law enforcement officials said on Monday.
CBS news and ABC news reported that a Cosby spokesman vehemently denied the woman was Cosby's daughter.
There is no evidence the blackmail attempt was related to the murder of Cosby's son, Mary Jo White, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, said in a prepared statement.

Autumn Jackson, 22, and Jose Medina, 51, were arrested on Saturday after they signed an agreement not to sell the story to tabloid newspapers in an office of a "representative" of the actor, said Joseph Valiquette, a spokesman for the New York FBI office.
The unnamed representative had gone to the FBI after the demands were made, he said.
